correctness.rationale: Stationary ON-edge count is Binomial(n,pi) at each fixed time. On O(n log n) horizon, integer-time Hoeffding and domination of unit-interval flips by a bounded-mean Poisson variable give uniform M(t)/n=pi+O(n^-1/3) with exceptional probability superpolynomially small. A single independent Poisson marked process per leaf realizes rate-one uniform-active selection and sandwiches contact times by independent gated clocks with mark rates c_n±/n. An ON/OFF killed chain has Q=[[-a,a],[b,-b-c]], survival A_c exp(-gamma_c t/n)+(1-A_c)exp(-Gamma_c t/n); at c=1/pi, A_c=(Gamma-1)/(Gamma-gamma)=C. IID extrema and smooth c_n±=c+o(1/log n) establish the full Gumbel center. Global mark intensity 1/n while ON dominates T_n and controls exceptional-event expectation; maxima have E=(n/gamma_c)(log(n A_c)+Euler)+o(n) uniformly. Differentiation of gamma²-(s+1/pi)gamma+s=0 gives gamma_prime>0. Independently cross-checked killed-generator survival by matrix exponential for five different a,b values. Analytical uniform tails rather than finite simulation justify the order-n expectation constant.

value.rationale: Fixed stationary availability can coexist with arbitrarily high serial contact-cover penalty due to persistence. The exact spectral gamma, nontrivial Gumbel center C and order-n mean refinement answer natural coverage deadline questions for hub collection with temporal ON/OFF gates, beyond generic n log n estimates.

final_claim: Under stationary independent slow ON/OFF edge switching at rates a/n,b/n on an n-leaf star, a unit-rate hub makes one uniformly active contact (with replacement) per event. The exact killed-gate principal exponent gamma and coefficient C give gamma*T_n/n-log(n C) => Gumbel and E T_n=(n/gamma)(log n+log C+Euler constant)+o(n); at fixed uptime, gamma increases strictly with switching speed.
limitations: Stationary independent links, rates a/n b/n with a,b fixed positive, rate-one serial hub contact with replacement; no general network or nonstationary/joint limit.
